artists.biography:
Amplifier are a progressive rock band from Manchester, England. The band has released four albums and two EPs since its inception in 1999. Their self-titled debut album was released in 2004 by Music for Nations. Their second album, Insider was released in Europe in 2006 on the SPV label. Their third album, The Octopus, was released to fans in December 2010 ahead of a full release in January 2011. The band's fourth album, Echo Street, was released in March 2013.

Amplifier's sound has been described as "Soundgarden, Tool, Black Sabbath, Oceansize and Pink Floyd taking copious amounts of mind-altering substances and venturing on a trip through time and space (to another dimension), and back again." Their music is characterised by lead singer and guitarist Balamir's effects pedals, extended heavy sections, atmospheric compositions and philosophical lyrics mainly dealing with astronomy, the cosmos and the darker side of human nature.

perplexity.description:
Amplifier's Hologram, released in 2023 on the Rockosmos label, marks the band's seventh studio album and their first new material since 2017. The album continues Amplifier's signature blend of psychedelic, space rock, and progressive rock, characterized by expansive soundscapes, atmospheric textures, and melodic guitar work. Tracks like "Two Way Mirror" and "Sweet Perfume" showcase the band's ability to merge introspective songwriting with driving rhythms and layered sonic experimentation, while the title track "Hologram" and "Tundra" further emphasize their affinity for immersive, otherworldly sound design.

Hologram stands as a pivotal release in Amplifier's discography, arriving after a period of relative quiet and following the departure of most original members, leaving founders Sel Balamir and Matt Brobin as the core of the band. The album was well-received by fans and critics alike, praised for its cohesive vision and the band's ability to evolve their sound while retaining their distinctive identity. Its release was accompanied by a strong promotional campaign, including an online premiere on the Rockosmos YouTube channel and a subsequent tour, reaffirming Amplifier's presence in the contemporary rock scene.
